lead: A memory chip holds many bytes, but it has only a few address pins. The CPU must pick one chip and then one byte inside it. Address decoding does that job. The high address lines are compared with a chosen base address. A decoder turns that match into a chip-select signal. The low lines go to the chip's address pins. This lets a 2K chip sit at 0000H and a RAM sit at 2000H without fighting on the bus. Every 8085 and 8086 system uses this idea.
prereq: You need: Chapter 2.1 for the 8085 address, data and control buses and Chapter 2.2 for memory read and write machine cycles.

sections.h3: Memory map, chip select and address lines

blocks.text: A memory map is the list of address ranges given to each chip. The 8085 puts a 16-bit address on A15-A0, so it can name 2^16 = 65536 bytes. The 8086 uses 20 lines A19-A0 and names 2^20 = 1048576 bytes. Each chip gets a base address, the first address in its range. It also gets a size, the number of bytes it holds. The chip-select pin, usually written CS with a bar over it, is active low: 0 V selects the chip. All other chips keep their data pins in high impedance.

blocks.where: size is the number of bytes in the chip; n is the number of address lines wired to the chip; base is the first address; end is the last address.

blocks.text: A 2K × 8 chip has 2048 bytes and needs 11 address lines, because 2^11 = 2048. The low 11 lines A10-A0 go to the chip. The upper lines A15-A11 decide whether this chip is selected. For a ROM at 0000H, A15-A11 must be 00000. For a RAM at 2000H, A15-A11 must be 00100. The range of the ROM is 0000H to 07FFH. The range of the RAM is 2000H to 27FFH. The H suffix means hexadecimal.

A simple decoder is a NAND gate. Its inputs are the high address lines, some inverted. Its output is active-low CS: it goes to 0 only when the address matches the base pattern. An AND gate with an inverter on its output does the same job. A 3-to-8 decoder saves gates. The 74LS138 takes three select inputs A, B, C and produces eight active-low outputs Y0-Y7. C is the most significant select input. It has enable pins: G1 active high, G2A and G2B active low. When enabled, the binary code on CBA selects one Y output low. For the two chips here, wire A13 to A, A14 to B, A15 to C. Tie A12 to G2A and A11 to G2B. Tie G1 high. ROM code 000 gives Y0; RAM code 001 gives Y1.

items: Full decoding uses every unused high address line. Each byte has one address. The map has no holes or copies.
Partial decoding leaves some high lines unconnected. The same chip appears at many addresses. This is called foldback or mirroring. It is cheaper but wastes address space.

In an 8086 system the memory is two byte banks. BHE low selects the high bank and A0 low selects the low bank. The decoder still compares the high address lines with the base address. A 2K chip still needs 11 address lines.

sections.h3: Interfacing a ROM and a RAM to the 8085

items: Connect A10-A0 of the 8085 to A10-A0 of both the 2K EPROM and the 2K RAM. These lines choose the byte inside each chip.
Connect D7-D0 of the 8085 to D7-D0 of both chips. Only the selected chip drives the data bus.
Decode A15-A11. Use a 74LS138 or gates to make ROM CS low for 0000H-07FFH and RAM CS low for 2000H-27FFH.

Make a memory-read signal MEMR = RD OR IO/M. MEMR is low only when RD is low and IO/M is low. Connect MEMR to the ROM OE and the RAM OE. In the same way make MEMW = WR OR IO/M and connect it to the RAM WE. OE and WE are active low. The EPROM has no write enable.
At reset the 8085 starts at 0000H. It fetches the first instruction from the EPROM. The RAM at 2000H is free for variables and stack.

figure.caption: The address bus feeds a 74LS138 decoder. Its outputs select the EPROM at 0000H-07FFH and the RAM at 2000H-27FFH; both share the data bus D7-D0.

spec.title: Address decoding for ROM and RAM
spec.aria: Address bus A15-A0 enters the 74LS138 decoder, whose outputs select the ROM at 0000H-07FFH and RAM at 2000H-27FFH; both chips connect to data bus D7-D0.

examples.question: Interface a 2K × 8 EPROM and a 2K × 8 RAM to an 8085. The EPROM starts at 0000H and the RAM starts at 2000H. Give the address range of each chip and the number of address lines each chip needs.
steps: Size of each chip = 2K × 8 = 2048 bytes × 8 bits.
Number of address lines n: 2^n = 2048, so n = log₂(2048) = 11. Each chip needs A10-A0, that is 11 address lines.
ROM base = 0000H. End = 0000H + 2048 − 1 = 0000H + 07FFH = 07FFH. ROM range = 0000H-07FFH. In decimal: 0 to 2047.
RAM base = 2000H. End = 2000H + 2048 − 1 = 2000H + 07FFH = 27FFH. RAM range = 2000H-27FFH. In decimal: 8192 to 10239.
Chip-select condition: ROM CS is low when A15-A11 = 00000. RAM CS is low when A15-A11 = 00100. A12 and A11 must be 0 for both; A13 separates the two chips.
examples.answer: Each chip holds 2048 bytes and needs 11 address lines; the EPROM covers 0000H-07FFH (0-2047 decimal) and the RAM covers 2000H-27FFH (8192-10239 decimal).
examples.check:
size = 2 * 1024
n = 0
while 2 ** n < size:
    n += 1
rom_start = 0x0000
ram_start = 0x2000
rom_end = rom_start + size - 1
ram_end = ram_start + size - 1
print(size)
print(n)
print(rom_start)
print(rom_end)
print(ram_start)
print(ram_end)

traps: A 2K chip needs 11 address lines, not 10. 2K = 2048 = 2^11.
The end address is base + size − 1. For a 2K chip starting at 2000H, the end is 27FFH, not 2800H.
H means hexadecimal, not a variable. 2000H is 8192 decimal.
Active-low CS is selected by logic 0. A high on CS deselects the chip.
Partial decoding gives mirror addresses; full decoding does not. The examiner often asks which lines must match.

quiz.a: CS is an active-low input that enables a memory chip to drive or accept data.

quiz.q: Why are high address lines decoded instead of low lines?
quiz.a: Low lines choose a byte inside the chip; high lines choose which chip. Decoding low lines would change chip selection for every byte.

quiz.q: A 4K × 8 RAM starts at 8000H. Find its range and address lines.
Two 2K chips are decoded using only A15 and A14; A13, A12 and A11 are left out. What problem occurs, and which line separates them?
quiz.a: Each chip appears at several ranges because A13-A11 are ignored. If the chips are meant to be at 0000H and 2000H, both respond when A15A14 = 00, so both can be selected together and fight on the data bus. Decode A13 to separate them.
It is a 3-to-8 decoder. One of eight active-low outputs is selected by CBA when enabled.

quiz.q: Why connect D7-D0 of both chips to the same data bus?
quiz.a: Only the selected chip drives the bus. The others stay in high impedance, so there is no conflict.

quiz.q: An 8086 has A19-A0. A 2K chip starts at 30000H. Find its range and address lines.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern systems put memory and registers in one address space, so the same decoder ideas map peripherals as if they were memory. FPGA and SoC designs often replace the 74LS138 with a small address decoder in hardware description language. Search for 'memory-mapped I/O', 'chip select generation' and 'address decoder Verilog' to go further.
